chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Mansur said:
I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who made a vow to fast but became unable to do so, so he said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: Upon him is a mud [of food] for each day.'

key_terms.اَلرِّضَا: Al-Rida (Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific unit of volume for food measurement

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a failed vow to fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the specific fidya for an unfulfilled fasting vow, attributing the ruling of feeding one mud of food per day to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of tracing legal precedents through the Imams, linking the practical expiation directly to the Prophet's household. It serves as a key reference for determining the quantity of food required when a vow of fasting becomes impossible to fulfill.
